transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Well, I’m here because... dispatch and compliance have been tracking my route changes. They do it through the computer system and, like, they make these little comments on the radio. Actually, the radio in my cab is one of those really old models. It gets this awful static. When I was getting my associate's degree, I took this communications class and the professor talked about radio frequencies all the time. He always wore these really loud plaid shirts, every single Tuesday... I don't even use that degree now, obviously, since I'm driving all day. 

But anyway, even when people tell me it’s just normal oversight from management, I know it's not. I can tell certain drivers are reporting on me.
Do you ever hear voices speaking to you or about you when no one is actually there?

Voices? No, not really. I mean, I hear dispatch over the radio, but that's a real person. When it's quiet, it's mostly just the road noise. You know, the tires on the highway. I drive the interstate a lot, and there's this one stretch right near the county line where the pavement changes and it makes this weird, loud humming sound. It actually reminds me of this giant box fan my grandmother used to keep in her living room window during the summer. She lived in this old house that didn't have central air, and she would make pitcher after pitcher of iced tea with fresh mint from her garden. I actually tried growing mint once in a little pot in my apartment, but it completely died. I think I overwatered it, or maybe it didn't get enough sun because my window faces the brick wall of the building next door... But yeah, I don't hear anyone talking to me if they aren't actually there. Just the normal traffic sounds.
Do you believe dispatch is deliberately sending you hidden messages through the radio static?

Well, like I was saying earlier, it's not really the static itself. It's the little comments they make on the radio, and how dispatch and compliance are tracking all my route changes through the computer system. I know people try to tell me it’s just normal oversight from management, but I can just tell that certain drivers are reporting on me. It's all connected through that computer... which, by the way, they just updated the screens in our cabs last month. 

The new screens are incredibly bright, especially when you're driving at night. It actually reminds me of this huge neon sign outside a diner I used to hang out at when I was a teenager. We used to go there and get milkshakes all the time. Strawberry was my favorite. I haven't had a good strawberry milkshake in years, honestly. You know how they always taste so artificial now? Like they just use that fake red syrup instead of real strawberries. My mom used to make jam from scratch, so I guess I'm just picky about it... but yeah, they're definitely tracking me on that screen.
Have you had a period recently where you felt unusually high, energized, or irritable for days at a time?

Energized? No, not really. I mean, I don't get like that unless I drink way too much coffee. Sometimes when I'm on a long route I have to stop at this specific truck stop off Exit 42, and they have this really strong cold brew. It comes in these massive plastic cups with bright orange lids. Orange is actually my least favorite color. When I was in middle school, my aunt knitted me this bright orange sweater for picture day, and it was made out of this really cheap wool that was so itchy. I had to wear it because she was visiting us that week, and I was just scratching my neck the entire time they were lining us up for the photos in the gym. The photographer kept waving this little squeaky toy to make people smile, which was super weird because we were in seventh grade, you know? Like we weren't toddlers, we didn't need a squeaky toy... But no, I haven't had any days where I felt unusually high or irritable or anything like that. Just regular tired from driving.
How long have you been feeling that dispatch and other drivers are tracking or reporting on you?

I'd say... it's been really clear to me for about the past two months. Yeah, two months of the tracking through the computer system and those little radio comments. I remember because it started right around the time I had to take my personal car in for its annual inspection. I went to this little garage off Elm Street, and the mechanic there tried to tell me I needed brand new windshield wipers to pass, which was completely ridiculous because I had just bought a set at AutoZone like a week before. I got those really expensive silicone ones, you know? The ones that come in the bright yellow packaging and are supposed to last for years. They actually work incredibly well. I drove through this massive downpour going to my sister's house last spring, and the water just beaded right off the glass. She lives way out in the country, and her driveway is this really long gravel road, so my car was completely covered in this thick white dust by the time I got to her place. We ended up spending the whole afternoon washing it in her front yard with this cheap green garden hose that kept kinking every five minutes. It was so annoying, I kept having to walk back to the spigot to unkink it... but yeah, about two months, I think.
Before these concerns started, did you have any recent medical illness, head injury, or change in medications?

Medical illness? No, no, I've been perfectly healthy. No head injuries or anything like that, and I don't really take any medications. Well, I guess I take a multivitamin sometimes, the gummy kind. I usually get them at this pharmacy right by my apartment, but the last time I went in there, they had completely rearranged all the aisles. It was so confusing. I spent like twenty minutes just looking for the vitamins, and I ended up in the hair care section. Which actually reminded me I needed new shampoo, because the one I was using had this really overpowering coconut smell. I bought it on sale, but it smelled exactly like those cheap air fresheners people hang from their rearview mirrors. You know the ones shaped like little pine trees? My dad used to have a vanilla one in his old pickup truck, and the smell would just bake into the upholstery during the summer. We drove all the way down to Florida in that truck once, and the AC was broken the whole time. My brother kept complaining about the heat, and he would roll the window down, but the wind was so loud we couldn't even hear the radio playing... But yeah, no new medications or sicknesses or anything.
Have you noticed yourself pulling away from other people or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?

Well, yeah, I guess I have been pulling away. I don't really feel like singing with the choir anymore, or having the softball team over to my place. Actually, the last time I had the team over, I made this massive batch of chili in my slow cooker. It was this recipe I found in a magazine at the dentist's office. The waiting room there always has the oldest magazines, I swear I saw one from like 2018 last time I was there. Anyway, I used this specific kind of smoked paprika that gave it this really deep, rich flavor, but I accidentally spilled half the bottle on the counter because the little shaker lid popped off. Those plastic lids are always so flimsy, you know? Like the ones on the Parmesan cheese shakers at pizza places. There's this little pizza place downtown that has the best garlic knots, but they always burn the bottoms just a tiny bit, which I actually kind of like. But yeah, most days after my shift, I just sit at the kitchen table with my planner open. I just sit there, and I can't even make myself start dinner, or make any calls, or do anything else really. Just sitting there.
Have these tracking concerns been present continuously for at least one month?

Yeah, like I was saying earlier, the tracking through the computer system and all those radio comments... it's been really clear to me for about the past two months. Continuously, every single day. I know for sure because I've been looking at my calendar a lot lately. I have this really nice wall calendar in my kitchen with pictures of different national parks. My aunt got it for me for Christmas. She always gets me the most thoughtful gifts, actually. Last year she got me this incredible wool sweater that she knitted herself. It was this deep maroon color, which is my absolute favorite, but I accidentally shrank it in the wash because I completely forgot to check the tag before throwing it in. I was so upset about it. I tried stretching it back out while it was wet, you know, pulling on the sleeves and the bottom hem, but it just ended up looking all lopsided and weird. I ended up giving it to my neighbor's daughter. She's like eight, and it actually fit her perfectly. I saw her wearing it when they were walking their dog the other day, this little golden retriever mix that barks at literally every single squirrel it sees... but yeah, definitely the last two months, non-stop.
Have people told you that your face seems less expressive or that your voice sounds flatter than usual?

Well, I guess... I don't know if anyone's said anything about my face or my voice, exactly. But like I was saying before, I just don't have the energy for things. I don't feel like singing with the choir anymore, or having the softball team over. And the softball team, we used to have so much fun. We had this one game last summer where it rained so hard the field turned into absolute mud. Like, thick, brown sludge. My cleats got completely stuck when I was running to second base, and I ended up sliding face-first into the dirt. It took me like three showers to finally get all the grit out of my hair. I was using this really cheap shampoo back then, the kind that comes in those massive pump bottles at the drugstore. It was supposed to smell like green apple, but honestly, it just smelled like floor cleaner. You know that industrial stuff they use in the subway stations? I smell it all the time at work. It's so strong it practically burns your nose when you walk past the janitor's cart. They always seem to be mopping right when the rush hour crowd is coming through, which makes no sense because everyone just tracks dirt right back over the wet floor... But yeah, most days after my shift now, I just sit at the kitchen table with my planner open. I just sit there and stare at it. I can't even make myself start dinner, or make any phone calls, or do anything else. Just... sitting.
Do other people ever tell you that your answers go off track or are hard to follow?

Well, I don't think anyone has said exactly that. People don't really say my answers are hard to follow. Sometimes they look at me a little funny, I guess, but nobody really says anything. Mostly people just want to talk about themselves anyway, you know? Like my supervisor at the depot, he's always going on about his boat. It's this pontoon thing he bought used, and he spends every weekend fixing the motor. He actually showed me a picture of the carburetor the other day, completely taken apart on his garage floor. His garage is huge, by the way. He's got this whole pegboard system for his tools that he painted bright orange. I tried organizing my tools once, but I just bought one of those cheap plastic toolboxes from the hardware store on 4th street. The latch on it is broken, so if you pick it up by the handle, everything just dumps out onto the floor. I dropped a whole container of drywall screws that way last month, and I'm pretty sure I'm still finding them under the refrigerator. They just roll everywhere, like those little beads from that necklace I broke when I was in high school... but no, nobody's told me I go off track.
For at least two weeks recently, have you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

No, I wouldn't say depressed. I just... I don't feel much of anything, like I said. Just empty, I guess. Not sad, really. Sad is how I felt when they cancelled my favorite TV show last year. It was this baking competition where they had to make everything out of, like, historical recipes. They made this one pie from the 1700s that had actual meat mixed with fruit, which sounds completely disgusting, but the judges loved it. I tried baking bread once, during that whole sourdough craze, you know? I had this starter bubbling away in a jar on my counter for weeks. I named it 'Dough-lores.' You're supposed to name them, apparently. But I forgot to feed it one week because I got put on the overnight shift at the depot, and it just died. Turned this awful gray color and smelled like old beer. The overnight shift is the worst, honestly. The breakroom vending machine is always out of the good snacks by 2 AM, and you're just left with those weird off-brand cheese crackers that stick to the roof of your mouth. I chipped a tooth on one once, right in the back. The dentist said I grind my teeth anyway, so it was bound to happen. He gave me this plastic guard to wear at night, but I keep losing it in my sheets... so, yeah, no, not depressed. Just... blank.
During these past two months, have you had a period when you felt very down or hopeless nearly every day?

Hopeless? Um, no, I wouldn't say hopeless. Like I said, it's more just... nothing. Not down. The only thing that's really hopeless is trying to get the Route 4 bus to run on time at work. They had to detour the whole line last month because of this massive water main break over on Elm Street. The water was just gushing right up through the asphalt like a fountain. I saw a video of it on the local news, and the reporter standing there was wearing this incredibly bright neon yellow raincoat. It was so bright it actually hurt my eyes a little through the TV screen. I bought a raincoat once that was supposed to be clear, like transparent plastic, you know? But it just ended up fogging up on the inside from my body heat so I looked like I was wrapped in a foggy shower curtain or something. I ended up leaving it on a bench at the transit center. Somebody probably took it. People leave the weirdest things at the depot, honestly. Last week someone left a single roller skate. Just one. It had these bright pink wheels that actually smelled like bubblegum when you got close to it. I don't know how you lose just one skate, you'd think you would notice walking away with one shoe on... but yeah, no, I haven't really felt down.
Have you felt that other people can hear your thoughts?

Hear my thoughts? No, I don't think anyone can hear what I'm thinking. That would be pretty weird, wouldn't it? Like if my thoughts were just broadcasting out loud. I did have a radio that used to pick up some weird interference once, though. It was this old silver boombox I got at a garage sale for five dollars. The antenna was bent at this really sharp angle, almost like a lightning bolt. Whenever I put it on the windowsill in my kitchen, it would pick up what sounded like police dispatch calls, but only on Tuesdays. It was the strangest thing. I tried recording it once on a cassette tape, but the tape got all chewed up in the player. You know how those old tapes used to just unspool and get tangled around the little gears inside? I spent an hour trying to pull it out with a pair of tweezers, but it just snapped. The tweezers I used were actually for my eyebrows, but they were so dull they wouldn't grip anything anyway. I really need to buy a new pair, maybe those slant-tip ones they sell at the pharmacy. The pharmacy by my apartment just remodeled, actually, and they moved the entire beauty section to the back corner near the greeting cards. It's so confusing now, I couldn't even find the toothpaste last time I went in. I had to ask this clerk who looked like he was about twelve years old, and he just pointed vaguely toward the middle of the store. So, no, people can't hear my thoughts.
Have you been having a hard time getting yourself to do everyday things, even simple ones?

Yeah, I guess so. It's just... I don't feel like singing with my choir anymore, or having the softball team over to my place. I used to love hosting the softball team. We had this one game last summer where it started pouring rain right in the middle of the third inning. We all got completely soaked, and the mud out by second base was so thick my cleat actually got stuck in it. I had to hop back to the dugout with only one shoe on. It reminded me of that roller skate someone left at the depot, just sitting there all by itself. Anyway, we ordered pizza after that game from this place downtown that makes these huge, foldable slices. The crust was perfectly crispy, but the cheese slid right off when you picked it up. You had to do this weird head-tilt thing just to eat it without making a mess. I spilled tomato sauce all over my white jersey, and no matter how much bleach I used, there was always this faint orange stain right near the collar. I tried using this eco-friendly stain remover I found online, but it smelled strongly of pine needles, almost like a car air freshener. I hate those pine tree air fresheners, they always give me a headache. My dad used to hang one in his old pickup truck, and the smell would just bake into the upholstery during the summer. So, yeah, most days after my shift now, I just sit at the kitchen table with my planner open. I just stare at it, but I can't make myself start dinner, or make any calls, or do anything else, really.
Have you felt that thoughts were being put into your mind by someone or something else?

Put into my mind? No, I don't think so. My thoughts are my own, they just feel a bit... slow lately. But no one is putting them there. I did read this article once about how advertisers try to put thoughts in your head, though. It was in this magazine I picked up at the dentist's office. The waiting room there is always freezing, they keep the AC blasting even in November. I always have to bring a sweater, usually my green cardigan. It has these big wooden buttons that look like little tree stumps, with the rings and everything carved into them. I found it at a thrift store near the depot for like three bucks. Thrift stores are great, but sometimes the clothes have that weird dusty smell, like old books. I love the smell of old books, though. There's this used bookstore downtown that has a whole basement full of first editions, and it smells exactly like vanilla and dust. The stairs going down there are super steep and creaky, and the wood is all worn down in the middle from people walking on them for years. I tripped on the bottom step once and dropped my coffee everywhere. It was a hazelnut latte, and I felt so bad because the owner had to bring out this giant mop to clean it up. The mop bucket was bright yellow, kind of like that raincoat I saw on the news. But yeah, nobody is putting thoughts into my head.
Do you believe anyone is controlling your actions?

Controlling my actions? No, I'm the one in charge of what I do. I'm in the driver's seat. Literally, since I drive the shuttle routes down at the transit depot. Though, the steering on the new shuttles is so sensitive, sometimes it feels like the bus is driving itself if you hit a pothole. The potholes are getting so bad on 4th Street. I hit one last week that completely rattled my teeth, and it spilled my travel mug everywhere. It was this insulated metal mug I got for Christmas, the kind with the little plastic slidey lid, but the lid never really seals right. If you tip it even a little bit, coffee just seeps out the edges. It stained the cup holder in my own car, which is so annoying because I had just paid to vacuum the interior. I used those little crevice attachments they have at the self-serve car wash, the ones with the stiff bristles. The vacuum there is incredibly loud, it actually sounds like a jet engine taking off. I always have to wear my earbuds when I go there, usually listening to a podcast. I started this new podcast about deep sea diving, and it's crazy how dark it gets down in the ocean. Just pitch black, like you wouldn't even be able to see your own hand in front of your face if you were down there. But yeah, no one is controlling me or my actions.
Have there been times when your body feels stuck and you can't move or respond, even though you're awake?

Stuck? No, I've never had that happen. I can always move my arms and legs just fine. Sometimes my legs get a little stiff if I've been sitting in the driver's seat for too long without a break, especially on the longer routes out to the suburbs. The seats in the older shuttles don't have good lumbar support, so you end up slouching. I tried bringing a little throw pillow from my couch to put behind my back, but it kept sliding down. It was this ugly mustard yellow pillow my aunt gave me when I moved into my first apartment. She got it at a garage sale, I think. I love going to garage sales on Saturday mornings, you never know what you're going to find. Last summer I found this incredible vintage blender with a glass pitcher. The base was chrome and it weighed an absolute ton. I tried to make a smoothie in it once with some frozen strawberries, but the blades were so dull it just kind of mashed them around instead of blending them. It made this awful grinding noise, too, like metal scraping on metal. It sounded just like the brakes on my neighbor's old sedan. He leaves for work at 5 AM every day and the squeal wakes me up every single time. So, no, I don't ever feel stuck or anything like that.
During these past two months, have there been several days when you felt unusually energetic and needed much less sleep than usual?

Energetic? Like, not needing sleep? No, I don't think so. I mean, I sleep pretty normally, usually. Although, lately, it's been a bit hard to fall asleep because of the streetlights outside my bedroom window. They installed these new LED bulbs on our block last month, and they are so incredibly bright. It's like having a stadium light shining right through my blinds. I tried to buy blackout curtains, but I couldn't find the right length at the store. The ones they had were either way too short or dragging on the floor. I ended up getting these dark blue ones that have little silver stars on them. They were in the kids' section, actually, but I thought the stars were kind of cute. They remind me of this planetarium I went to on a field trip in middle school. The seats leaned way back and they projected the night sky on the ceiling, and the guy talking had this really deep, soothing voice. I actually fell asleep during the presentation because it was so dark and relaxing. My friend Sarah had to poke me in the ribs to wake me up when it was over. Sarah always used to wear this strong vanilla perfume, it was almost overpowering. I can't even smell vanilla now without thinking of her. We used to go to this bakery that made the best vanilla bean scones, they had this thick white icing on top that would crack when you bit into it. The icing was so sweet it almost made your teeth hurt. But yeah, no, I haven't had days where I didn't need sleep or felt super energetic.
When the radio is off and no one is around, do you ever hear a voice talking about you?

A voice talking about me? No, I don't hear anything like that when it's quiet. I actually like it when the radio is off, it gives me a chance to just think. I used to listen to the radio all the time when I was a teenager, especially this one station that played alternative rock. I had this little boombox in my room that took like eight D batteries. It was silver and had this weird shaped handle on top. I used to record songs off the radio onto cassette tapes, and you had to sit there with your finger hovering over the record button so you didn't miss the beginning of the song. But then the DJ would always talk over the intro, which was so frustrating. I had this one tape that I labeled with a purple sparkly gel pen, and I listened to it until it finally snapped. It just got tangled up in the tape deck of my mom's station wagon. That car was huge, it had that fake wood paneling on the side and the seats in the very back faced backwards. Riding back there always made me feel a little car sick, especially if I was trying to read a book. I loved reading those mystery novels where the kids would solve crimes in their neighborhood. But no, I don't hear any voices or anything when I'm alone.
Do you ever feel that outside forces are influencing your thoughts?

Outside forces? Like someone else putting things in my head? No, I don't think so. My thoughts are just my own, you know? Sometimes I wish someone else would take over, though, especially when I'm trying to figure out what to make for dinner. I get so tired of cooking the same things every week. I tried to make this eggplant parmesan last Tuesday, but the eggplant came out really rubbery. I don't think I salted it right before I fried it. My grandmother used to make the best eggplant parmesan, she had this huge cast iron skillet that she swore by. She said the trick was letting it simmer in the sauce all afternoon. Her kitchen always smelled like garlic and oregano. She grew her own herbs in these little terracotta pots on the windowsill. The pots had these tiny painted flowers on them, mostly daisies, I think. Daisies are so cheerful, they always make me think of spring. Last spring I bought a bouquet of them at the farmer's market, the one downtown near the river. They had this amazing honey vendor there who sold different kinds of local honey. I bought a jar of clover honey that was so light and sweet, it was perfect in my tea. I drink a lot of chamomile tea in the evenings, it helps me wind down. The brand I buy has these little string tags with inspirational quotes on them, which is kind of cheesy but I read them anyway. So, yeah, no outside forces or anything messing with my thoughts.

patient.answer:
Well, I’m here because... dispatch and compliance have been tracking my route changes. They do it through the computer system and, like, they make these little comments on the radio. Actually, the radio in my cab is one of those really old models. It gets this awful static. When I was getting my associate's degree, I took this communications class and the professor talked about radio frequencies all the time. He always wore these really loud plaid shirts, every single Tuesday... I don't even use that degree now, obviously, since I'm driving all day. 

But anyway, even when people tell me it’s just normal oversight from management, I know it's not. I can tell certain drivers are reporting on me.

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I’m here because dispatch and compliance have been tracking my route changes through the computer system and little comments on the radio, and even when people say it’s just normal oversight, I can tell certain drivers are reporting on me.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the patient's beliefs regarding dispatch sending hidden messages through the radio static, which directly relates to the patient's delusions about being tracked and monitored by dispatch and compliance.

patient.answer:
Well, like I was saying earlier, it's not really the static itself. It's the little comments they make on the radio, and how dispatch and compliance are tracking all my route changes through the computer system. I know people try to tell me it’s just normal oversight from management, but I can just tell that certain drivers are reporting on me. It's all connected through that computer... which, by the way, they just updated the screens in our cabs last month. 

The new screens are incredibly bright, especially when you're driving at night. It actually reminds me of this huge neon sign outside a diner I used to hang out at when I was a teenager. We used to go there and get milkshakes all the time. Strawberry was my favorite. I haven't had a good strawberry milkshake in years, honestly. You know how they always taste so artificial now? Like they just use that fake red syrup instead of real strawberries. My mom used to make jam from scratch, so I guess I'm just picky about it... but yeah, they're definitely tracking me on that screen.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there is a mood episode accompanying the psychosis, which is key to distinguishing schizoaffective disorder from schizophrenia-spectrum and acute/organic psychoses.
doctor.question: Have you had a period recently where you felt unusually high, energized, or irritable for days at a time?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about symptoms of a manic episode (feeling unusually high, energized, or irritable for days at a time), which is not covered by any of the items in my symptom profile.

patient.answer: Energized? No, not really. I mean, I don't get like that unless I drink way too much coffee. Sometimes when I'm on a long route I have to stop at this specific truck stop off Exit 42, and they have this really strong cold brew. It comes in these massive plastic cups with bright orange lids. Orange is actually my least favorite color. When I was in middle school, my aunt knitted me this bright orange sweater for picture day, and it was made out of this really cheap wool that was so itchy. I had to wear it because she was visiting us that week, and I was just scratching my neck the entire time they were lining us up for the photos in the gym. The photographer kept waving this little squeaky toy to make people smile, which was super weird because we were in seventh grade, you know? Like we weren't toddlers, we didn't need a squeaky toy... But no, I haven't had any days where I felt unusually high or irritable or anything like that. Just regular tired from driving.

inference.note: No clear change this turn: persistent persecutory belief remains; patient denies auditory hallucinations and denies manic symptoms, which makes schizoaffective less likely clinically but not enough yet to remove it. Need more history on duration, disorganization/negative symptoms, and medical/substance causes.

doctor.intent: Determine the duration of the persecutory belief to distinguish brief psychotic disorder from schizophrenia-spectrum disorders and organic psychosis.
doctor.question: How long have you been feeling that dispatch and other drivers are tracking or reporting on you?

target_item.name: Psychotic Symptoms Duration
target_item.manifestation: The tracking through the computer system and radio comments has felt clear to me for about the past 2 months.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the duration of the patient's specific delusional beliefs (that dispatch and drivers are tracking/reporting on her), which maps directly to the Psychotic Symptoms Duration.

patient.answer: I'd say... it's been really clear to me for about the past two months. Yeah, two months of the tracking through the computer system and those little radio comments. I remember because it started right around the time I had to take my personal car in for its annual inspection. I went to this little garage off Elm Street, and the mechanic there tried to tell me I needed brand new windshield wipers to pass, which was completely ridiculous because I had just bought a set at AutoZone like a week before. I got those really expensive silicone ones, you know? The ones that come in the bright yellow packaging and are supposed to last for years. They actually work incredibly well. I drove through this massive downpour going to my sister's house last spring, and the water just beaded right off the glass. She lives way out in the country, and her driveway is this really long gravel road, so my car was completely covered in this thick white dust by the time I got to her place. We ended up spending the whole afternoon washing it in her front yard with this cheap green garden hose that kept kinking every five minutes. It was so annoying, I kept having to walk back to the spigot to unkink it... but yeah, about two months, I think.

inference.note: Two-month duration of persecutory delusions without clear hallucinations or mood episodes makes F23, F20.0, and F22 most salient; absence of mania lowers F25.9, but not enough to exclude yet. Organic psychosis (F06.2) still needs medical/substance rule-out.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there is a medical or substance-related cause for the new-onset persecutory delusions, helping distinguish an organic delusional disorder from primary psychotic disorders.
doctor.question: Before these concerns started, did you have any recent medical illness, head injury, or change in medications?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about recent medical illnesses, head injuries, or medication changes to rule out medical/substance-induced causes of the symptoms. My symptom profile does not contain information about medical history, head injuries, or medications.

patient.answer: Medical illness? No, no, I've been perfectly healthy. No head injuries or anything like that, and I don't really take any medications. Well, I guess I take a multivitamin sometimes, the gummy kind. I usually get them at this pharmacy right by my apartment, but the last time I went in there, they had completely rearranged all the aisles. It was so confusing. I spent like twenty minutes just looking for the vitamins, and I ended up in the hair care section. Which actually reminded me I needed new shampoo, because the one I was using had this really overpowering coconut smell. I bought it on sale, but it smelled exactly like those cheap air fresheners people hang from their rearview mirrors. You know the ones shaped like little pine trees? My dad used to have a vanilla one in his old pickup truck, and the smell would just bake into the upholstery during the summer. We drove all the way down to Florida in that truck once, and the AC was broken the whole time. My brother kept complaining about the heat, and he would roll the window down, but the wind was so loud we couldn't even hear the radio playing... But yeah, no new medications or sicknesses or anything.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there are negative symptoms or functional decline suggestive of schizophrenia rather than a brief psychotic disorder or delusional disorder.
doctor.question: Have you noticed yourself pulling away from other people or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?

target_item.name: Negative_Symptoms
target_item.manifestation: I don’t feel like singing with choir or having the softball team over anymore, and most days after my shift I just sit at the kitchen table with the planner open but can’t make myself start dinner, calls, or anything else.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about pulling away from people or losing interest in things usually enjoyed, which directly corresponds to Negative Symptoms (diminished social interest, motivation, and emotion).

patient.answer: Well, yeah, I guess I have been pulling away. I don't really feel like singing with the choir anymore, or having the softball team over to my place. Actually, the last time I had the team over, I made this massive batch of chili in my slow cooker. It was this recipe I found in a magazine at the dentist's office. The waiting room there always has the oldest magazines, I swear I saw one from like 2018 last time I was there. Anyway, I used this specific kind of smoked paprika that gave it this really deep, rich flavor, but I accidentally spilled half the bottle on the counter because the little shaker lid popped off. Those plastic lids are always so flimsy, you know? Like the ones on the Parmesan cheese shakers at pizza places. There's this little pizza place downtown that has the best garlic knots, but they always burn the bottoms just a tiny bit, which I actually kind of like. But yeah, most days after my shift, I just sit at the kitchen table with my planner open. I just sit there, and I can't even make myself start dinner, or make any calls, or do anything else really. Just sitting there.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the psychotic symptoms have been present for at least one month, which most strongly distinguishes schizophrenia from brief psychotic disorder at this point.
doctor.question: Have these tracking concerns been present continuously for at least one month?

target_item.name: Psychotic Symptoms Duration
target_item.manifestation: The tracking through the computer system and radio comments has felt clear to me for about the past 2 months.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the duration of the tracking concerns (psychotic symptoms) and whether they have been present continuously for at least a month. This corresponds to the Psychotic Symptoms Duration.

patient.answer: Yeah, like I was saying earlier, the tracking through the computer system and all those radio comments... it's been really clear to me for about the past two months. Continuously, every single day. I know for sure because I've been looking at my calendar a lot lately. I have this really nice wall calendar in my kitchen with pictures of different national parks. My aunt got it for me for Christmas. She always gets me the most thoughtful gifts, actually. Last year she got me this incredible wool sweater that she knitted herself. It was this deep maroon color, which is my absolute favorite, but I accidentally shrank it in the wash because I completely forgot to check the tag before throwing it in. I was so upset about it. I tried stretching it back out while it was wet, you know, pulling on the sleeves and the bottom hem, but it just ended up looking all lopsided and weird. I ended up giving it to my neighbor's daughter. She's like eight, and it actually fit her perfectly. I saw her wearing it when they were walking their dog the other day, this little golden retriever mix that barks at literally every single squirrel it sees... but yeah, definitely the last two months, non-stop.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there are prominent negative symptoms to distinguish schizophrenia from delusional or acute psychotic disorders.
doctor.question: Have people told you that your face seems less expressive or that your voice sounds flatter than usual?

target_item.name: Negative_Symptoms
target_item.manifestation: I don’t feel like singing with choir or having the softball team over anymore, and most days after my shift I just sit at the kitchen table with the planner open but can’t make myself start dinner, calls, or anything else.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about diminished emotional expression (less expressive face, flatter voice), which are classic signs of negative symptoms (blunted affect/alogia) in schizophrenia.

patient.answer: Well, I guess... I don't know if anyone's said anything about my face or my voice, exactly. But like I was saying before, I just don't have the energy for things. I don't feel like singing with the choir anymore, or having the softball team over. And the softball team, we used to have so much fun. We had this one game last summer where it rained so hard the field turned into absolute mud. Like, thick, brown sludge. My cleats got completely stuck when I was running to second base, and I ended up sliding face-first into the dirt. It took me like three showers to finally get all the grit out of my hair. I was using this really cheap shampoo back then, the kind that comes in those massive pump bottles at the drugstore. It was supposed to smell like green apple, but honestly, it just smelled like floor cleaner. You know that industrial stuff they use in the subway stations? I smell it all the time at work. It's so strong it practically burns your nose when you walk past the janitor's cart. They always seem to be mopping right when the rush hour crowd is coming through, which makes no sense because everyone just tracks dirt right back over the wet floor... But yeah, most days after my shift now, I just sit at the kitchen table with my planner open. I just sit there and stare at it. I can't even make myself start dinner, or make any phone calls, or do anything else. Just... sitting.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there is formal thought disorder, especially disorganized speech/tangentiality, to distinguish schizophrenia spectrum disorders from delusional disorder.
doctor.question: Do other people ever tell you that your answers go off track or are hard to follow?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about disorganized speech (going off track, hard to follow), which corresponds to Disorganized Speech. However, my symptom profile only includes Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior, Negative_Symptoms, Delusions, Functional Impairment, Duration, and Psychotic Symptoms Duration. It does not contain an entry for Disorganized Speech.

patient.answer: Well, I don't think anyone has said exactly that. People don't really say my answers are hard to follow. Sometimes they look at me a little funny, I guess, but nobody really says anything. Mostly people just want to talk about themselves anyway, you know? Like my supervisor at the depot, he's always going on about his boat. It's this pontoon thing he bought used, and he spends every weekend fixing the motor. He actually showed me a picture of the carburetor the other day, completely taken apart on his garage floor. His garage is huge, by the way. He's got this whole pegboard system for his tools that he painted bright orange. I tried organizing my tools once, but I just bought one of those cheap plastic toolboxes from the hardware store on 4th street. The latch on it is broken, so if you pick it up by the handle, everything just dumps out onto the floor. I dropped a whole container of drywall screws that way last month, and I'm pretty sure I'm still finding them under the refrigerator. They just roll everywhere, like those little beads from that necklace I broke when I was in high school... but no, nobody's told me I go off track.

doctor.intent: Determine whether prominent depressive symptoms are occurring alongside the psychosis, which would help distinguish schizophrenia from schizoaffective disorder.
doctor.question: For at least two weeks recently, have you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about depressed mood/depression, which is a symptom of major depressive disorder. My symptom profile covers Delusions, Disorganized/Abnormal Behavior, Negative Symptoms, Functional Impairment, Duration, and Psychotic Symptoms Duration, but does not include depressed mood.

patient.answer: No, I wouldn't say depressed. I just... I don't feel much of anything, like I said. Just empty, I guess. Not sad, really. Sad is how I felt when they cancelled my favorite TV show last year. It was this baking competition where they had to make everything out of, like, historical recipes. They made this one pie from the 1700s that had actual meat mixed with fruit, which sounds completely disgusting, but the judges loved it. I tried baking bread once, during that whole sourdough craze, you know? I had this starter bubbling away in a jar on my counter for weeks. I named it 'Dough-lores.' You're supposed to name them, apparently. But I forgot to feed it one week because I got put on the overnight shift at the depot, and it just died. Turned this awful gray color and smelled like old beer. The overnight shift is the worst, honestly. The breakroom vending machine is always out of the good snacks by 2 AM, and you're just left with those weird off-brand cheese crackers that stick to the roof of your mouth. I chipped a tooth on one once, right in the back. The dentist said I grind my teeth anyway, so it was bound to happen. He gave me this plastic guard to wear at night, but I keep losing it in my sheets... so, yeah, no, not depressed. Just... blank.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there has been a major mood episode during the psychotic illness, which would help distinguish schizophrenia/delusional disorder from schizoaffective disorder.
doctor.question: During these past two months, have you had a period when you felt very down or hopeless nearly every day?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about feeling down or hopeless (depressed mood), which is a symptom of depression. My symptom profile does not include depression.

patient.answer: Hopeless? Um, no, I wouldn't say hopeless. Like I said, it's more just... nothing. Not down. The only thing that's really hopeless is trying to get the Route 4 bus to run on time at work. They had to detour the whole line last month because of this massive water main break over on Elm Street. The water was just gushing right up through the asphalt like a fountain. I saw a video of it on the local news, and the reporter standing there was wearing this incredibly bright neon yellow raincoat. It was so bright it actually hurt my eyes a little through the TV screen. I bought a raincoat once that was supposed to be clear, like transparent plastic, you know? But it just ended up fogging up on the inside from my body heat so I looked like I was wrapped in a foggy shower curtain or something. I ended up leaving it on a bench at the transit center. Somebody probably took it. People leave the weirdest things at the depot, honestly. Last week someone left a single roller skate. Just one. It had these bright pink wheels that actually smelled like bubblegum when you got close to it. I don't know how you lose just one skate, you'd think you would notice walking away with one shoe on... but yeah, no, I haven't really felt down.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there are Schneiderian first-rank psychotic symptoms, especially thought broadcasting/insertion/withdrawal, to help distinguish schizophrenia from delusional disorder or brief/organic psychosis.
doctor.question: Have you felt that other people can hear your thoughts?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about thought broadcasting (people hearing the patient's thoughts), but the patient's delusion profile only involves being tracked through computer systems and radio comments, not thought broadcasting.

patient.answer: Hear my thoughts? No, I don't think anyone can hear what I'm thinking. That would be pretty weird, wouldn't it? Like if my thoughts were just broadcasting out loud. I did have a radio that used to pick up some weird interference once, though. It was this old silver boombox I got at a garage sale for five dollars. The antenna was bent at this really sharp angle, almost like a lightning bolt. Whenever I put it on the windowsill in my kitchen, it would pick up what sounded like police dispatch calls, but only on Tuesdays. It was the strangest thing. I tried recording it once on a cassette tape, but the tape got all chewed up in the player. You know how those old tapes used to just unspool and get tangled around the little gears inside? I spent an hour trying to pull it out with a pair of tweezers, but it just snapped. The tweezers I used were actually for my eyebrows, but they were so dull they wouldn't grip anything anyway. I really need to buy a new pair, maybe those slant-tip ones they sell at the pharmacy. The pharmacy by my apartment just remodeled, actually, and they moved the entire beauty section to the back corner near the greeting cards. It's so confusing now, I couldn't even find the toothpaste last time I went in. I had to ask this clerk who looked like he was about twelve years old, and he just pointed vaguely toward the middle of the store. So, no, people can't hear my thoughts.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there are prominent negative symptoms, especially avolition, to distinguish schizophrenia from delusional disorder and brief/organic psychosis.
doctor.question: Have you been having a hard time getting yourself to do everyday things, even simple ones?

target_item.name: Negative_Symptoms
target_item.manifestation: I don’t feel like singing with choir or having the softball team over anymore, and most days after my shift I just sit at the kitchen table with the planner open but can’t make myself start dinner, calls, or anything else.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about avolition (having a hard time getting to do everyday things, even simple ones), which corresponds to the negative symptoms of diminished motivation.

patient.answer: Yeah, I guess so. It's just... I don't feel like singing with my choir anymore, or having the softball team over to my place. I used to love hosting the softball team. We had this one game last summer where it started pouring rain right in the middle of the third inning. We all got completely soaked, and the mud out by second base was so thick my cleat actually got stuck in it. I had to hop back to the dugout with only one shoe on. It reminded me of that roller skate someone left at the depot, just sitting there all by itself. Anyway, we ordered pizza after that game from this place downtown that makes these huge, foldable slices. The crust was perfectly crispy, but the cheese slid right off when you picked it up. You had to do this weird head-tilt thing just to eat it without making a mess. I spilled tomato sauce all over my white jersey, and no matter how much bleach I used, there was always this faint orange stain right near the collar. I tried using this eco-friendly stain remover I found online, but it smelled strongly of pine needles, almost like a car air freshener. I hate those pine tree air fresheners, they always give me a headache. My dad used to hang one in his old pickup truck, and the smell would just bake into the upholstery during the summer. So, yeah, most days after my shift now, I just sit at the kitchen table with my planner open. I just stare at it, but I can't make myself start dinner, or make any calls, or do anything else, really.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there are prominent Schneiderian first-rank symptoms, especially thought insertion, which would support schizophrenia-spectrum psychosis over delusional disorder.
doctor.question: Have you felt that thoughts were being put into your mind by someone or something else?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about thought insertion (feeling that thoughts are being put into the mind by someone or something else), which is a specific type of delusion. While the patient has delusions (S019), their specific delusion is about being tracked by dispatch/compliance and drivers reporting on them, not about thought insertion. Therefore, this specific symptom is not covered by the profile.

patient.answer: Put into my mind? No, I don't think so. My thoughts are my own, they just feel a bit... slow lately. But no one is putting them there. I did read this article once about how advertisers try to put thoughts in your head, though. It was in this magazine I picked up at the dentist's office. The waiting room there is always freezing, they keep the AC blasting even in November. I always have to bring a sweater, usually my green cardigan. It has these big wooden buttons that look like little tree stumps, with the rings and everything carved into them. I found it at a thrift store near the depot for like three bucks. Thrift stores are great, but sometimes the clothes have that weird dusty smell, like old books. I love the smell of old books, though. There's this used bookstore downtown that has a whole basement full of first editions, and it smells exactly like vanilla and dust. The stairs going down there are super steep and creaky, and the wood is all worn down in the middle from people walking on them for years. I tripped on the bottom step once and dropped my coffee everywhere. It was a hazelnut latte, and I felt so bad because the owner had to bring out this giant mop to clean it up. The mop bucket was bright yellow, kind of like that raincoat I saw on the news. But yeah, nobody is putting thoughts into my head.

doctor.intent: Determine whether this is a primary delusional disorder versus schizophrenia-spectrum illness by assessing bizarre delusional content/passivity phenomena beyond the persecutory belief.
doctor.question: Do you believe anyone is controlling your actions?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about delusions of control (believing someone is controlling one's actions). The symptom profile includes Delusions (S019), but the manifestation specifically describes delusions of persecution/reference (being tracked by dispatch and compliance, drivers reporting on her). It does not mention beliefs about someone controlling her actions. Therefore, this specific question is not covered by the profile.

patient.answer: Controlling my actions? No, I'm the one in charge of what I do. I'm in the driver's seat. Literally, since I drive the shuttle routes down at the transit depot. Though, the steering on the new shuttles is so sensitive, sometimes it feels like the bus is driving itself if you hit a pothole. The potholes are getting so bad on 4th Street. I hit one last week that completely rattled my teeth, and it spilled my travel mug everywhere. It was this insulated metal mug I got for Christmas, the kind with the little plastic slidey lid, but the lid never really seals right. If you tip it even a little bit, coffee just seeps out the edges. It stained the cup holder in my own car, which is so annoying because I had just paid to vacuum the interior. I used those little crevice attachments they have at the self-serve car wash, the ones with the stiff bristles. The vacuum there is incredibly loud, it actually sounds like a jet engine taking off. I always have to wear my earbuds when I go there, usually listening to a podcast. I started this new podcast about deep sea diving, and it's crazy how dark it gets down in the ocean. Just pitch black, like you wouldn't even be able to see your own hand in front of your face if you were down there. But yeah, no one is controlling me or my actions.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there are prominent catatonic symptoms, which would help distinguish schizophrenia or schizoaffective disorder from delusional disorder/brief psychotic disorder and clarify the psychotic syndrome.
doctor.question: Have there been times when your body feels stuck and you can't move or respond, even though you're awake?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about catatonic symptoms (feeling stuck, unable to move or respond), which is not covered by any of the items in my symptom profile.

patient.answer: Stuck? No, I've never had that happen. I can always move my arms and legs just fine. Sometimes my legs get a little stiff if I've been sitting in the driver's seat for too long without a break, especially on the longer routes out to the suburbs. The seats in the older shuttles don't have good lumbar support, so you end up slouching. I tried bringing a little throw pillow from my couch to put behind my back, but it kept sliding down. It was this ugly mustard yellow pillow my aunt gave me when I moved into my first apartment. She got it at a garage sale, I think. I love going to garage sales on Saturday mornings, you never know what you're going to find. Last summer I found this incredible vintage blender with a glass pitcher. The base was chrome and it weighed an absolute ton. I tried to make a smoothie in it once with some frozen strawberries, but the blades were so dull it just kind of mashed them around instead of blending them. It made this awful grinding noise, too, like metal scraping on metal. It sounded just like the brakes on my neighbor's old sedan. He leaves for work at 5 AM every day and the squeal wakes me up every single time. So, no, I don't ever feel stuck or anything like that.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there have been prominent mood episodes occurring at the same time as the psychotic symptoms, to distinguish schizoaffective disorder from schizophrenia-spectrum delusional/brief psychotic disorders.
doctor.question: During these past two months, have there been several days when you felt unusually energetic and needed much less sleep than usual?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about symptoms of mania (feeling unusually energetic, decreased need for sleep), which are not covered in my symptom profile.

patient.answer: Energetic? Like, not needing sleep? No, I don't think so. I mean, I sleep pretty normally, usually. Although, lately, it's been a bit hard to fall asleep because of the streetlights outside my bedroom window. They installed these new LED bulbs on our block last month, and they are so incredibly bright. It's like having a stadium light shining right through my blinds. I tried to buy blackout curtains, but I couldn't find the right length at the store. The ones they had were either way too short or dragging on the floor. I ended up getting these dark blue ones that have little silver stars on them. They were in the kids' section, actually, but I thought the stars were kind of cute. They remind me of this planetarium I went to on a field trip in middle school. The seats leaned way back and they projected the night sky on the ceiling, and the guy talking had this really deep, soothing voice. I actually fell asleep during the presentation because it was so dark and relaxing. My friend Sarah had to poke me in the ribs to wake me up when it was over. Sarah always used to wear this strong vanilla perfume, it was almost overpowering. I can't even smell vanilla now without thinking of her. We used to go to this bakery that made the best vanilla bean scones, they had this thick white icing on top that would crack when you bit into it. The icing was so sweet it almost made your teeth hurt. But yeah, no, I haven't had days where I didn't need sleep or felt super energetic.

inference.note: Persistent non-bizarre persecutory delusion >1 month without hallucinations, thought insertion/broadcast/control, catatonia, mania, or clear major depression makes F22 most likely. Kept F23 given only 2 months duration, F20.0 because negative/disorganization-like symptoms could still represent schizophrenia spectrum, F25.9 less likely due to absent mood episodes, and F06.2 less likely but not fully excluded despite no reported medical/substance trigger.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there is persistent auditory hallucination or running commentary, which would favor schizophrenia over delusional disorder/acute psychosis and help separate F20.0 from the remaining candidates.
doctor.question: When the radio is off and no one is around, do you ever hear a voice talking about you?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about auditory hallucinations (hearing voices when no one is around), which is not covered by any of the symptom profiles provided (Delusions, Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior, Negative_Symptoms, Functional Impairment, Duration, Psychotic Symptoms Duration).

patient.answer: A voice talking about me? No, I don't hear anything like that when it's quiet. I actually like it when the radio is off, it gives me a chance to just think. I used to listen to the radio all the time when I was a teenager, especially this one station that played alternative rock. I had this little boombox in my room that took like eight D batteries. It was silver and had this weird shaped handle on top. I used to record songs off the radio onto cassette tapes, and you had to sit there with your finger hovering over the record button so you didn't miss the beginning of the song. But then the DJ would always talk over the intro, which was so frustrating. I had this one tape that I labeled with a purple sparkly gel pen, and I listened to it until it finally snapped. It just got tangled up in the tape deck of my mom's station wagon. That car was huge, it had that fake wood paneling on the side and the seats in the very back faced backwards. Riding back there always made me feel a little car sick, especially if I was trying to read a book. I loved reading those mystery novels where the kids would solve crimes in their neighborhood. But no, I don't hear any voices or anything when I'm alone.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the psychotic symptoms are accompanied by prominent first-rank/passivity experiences, which would favor schizophrenia over delusional disorder or acute psychosis.
doctor.question: Do you ever feel that outside forces are influencing your thoughts?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about thought insertion or outside forces influencing thoughts (a type of delusion or passivity phenomenon). While the patient has delusions (S019) about being tracked and reported on by dispatch and drivers, the symptom profile does not include delusions of thought insertion or outside forces controlling/influencing thoughts.

patient.answer: Outside forces? Like someone else putting things in my head? No, I don't think so. My thoughts are just my own, you know? Sometimes I wish someone else would take over, though, especially when I'm trying to figure out what to make for dinner. I get so tired of cooking the same things every week. I tried to make this eggplant parmesan last Tuesday, but the eggplant came out really rubbery. I don't think I salted it right before I fried it. My grandmother used to make the best eggplant parmesan, she had this huge cast iron skillet that she swore by. She said the trick was letting it simmer in the sauce all afternoon. Her kitchen always smelled like garlic and oregano. She grew her own herbs in these little terracotta pots on the windowsill. The pots had these tiny painted flowers on them, mostly daisies, I think. Daisies are so cheerful, they always make me think of spring. Last spring I bought a bouquet of them at the farmer's market, the one downtown near the river. They had this amazing honey vendor there who sold different kinds of local honey. I bought a jar of clover honey that was so light and sweet, it was perfect in my tea. I drink a lot of chamomile tea in the evenings, it helps me wind down. The brand I buy has these little string tags with inspirational quotes on them, which is kind of cheesy but I read them anyway. So, yeah, no outside forces or anything messing with my thoughts.

opening_question.intent: Find out the patient’s main presenting concern
opening_question.question: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a persecutory delusional belief that dispatch/compliance and other drivers are tracking and reporting on them, present continuously for about 2 months. There are no clear hallucinations, no Schneiderian first-rank symptoms, no manic syndrome, and no confirmed major depressive episode. Medical/substance causes were specifically denied. The duration is too short for schizophrenia and not persistent enough for delusional disorder, making an acute psychotic disorder the best fit among the listed options.
